Resolves #18805

🌿 The corpus's ordinal conformance stops being a sentence someone once measured and becomes a number the repository can produce on demand — so the next reader never has to ask whether 175 is current, historical, or already repaired.

#16069 recorded 175 artifacts sitting where the archived-content layout contract would not place them, then was deprioritised behind the publisher gap. Its Fix section says the predicate is worth having **"either way"**, and that phrase is the whole warrant for this PR: deciding to soften the derivability claim still wants the number being softened.

Evidence: **L1** — a pure predicate over on-disk membership, measured green-at-head and red-under-two-mutations, plus one arm that exercises the real CLI against the committed corpus.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `findOrdinalMisplacements({archiveRoot})` exported and pure; families **and versions** derived from disk, so a bucket added later is measured with no edit here. Arm: *buckets are derived on BOTH levels* |
| AC-2 | report-only CLI mode prints the per-bucket table and exits 0. **Red control:** the arm runs the real guard against today's non-conforming corpus and asserts `status === 0` — a mode that failed a commit over pre-existing damage would wedge the repository |
| AC-3 | temp-corpus arms: a conforming bucket reports nothing across the 100/101 boundary; a misplaced artifact is reported **with the chunk it belongs in**; an id-less artifact is `unorderable` rather than ranked |
| AC-4 | the run below reproduces #16069's three buckets exactly, a month after it filed them |
| AC-5 | the duplicate check is untouched — `--all` exit 0, no-args exit 0, same staged-set semantics, same message. **After RA-2**: `--ordinals` no longer shares a run with it at all |

## Test Evidence

```
check-content-logical-identity --ordinals
  issues/v13.0.0    members= 1713   ADR shape=chunk-1..18   misplaced= 26
  pulls/v13.0.0     members= 1445   ADR shape=chunk-1..15   misplaced=119
  pulls/v13.1.0     members=  746   ADR shape=chunk-1..8    misplaced= 30
  175 total, exit 0

checkContentLogicalIdentity.spec           13 passed  (7 pre-existing + 6 new)
unit/buildScripts tier                    791 passed

mutation: ordinal floor(i/100) not +1       3 arms red   -> restored -> green
mutation: id-less artifact folded to 0      1 arm  red   -> restored -> green

RA-2, planted duplicate in archive/pulls/v13.0.0/chunk-2:
  before   --all exit 1   |   --all --ordinals exit 0    <- a reporting flag disabled a gate
  after    --all exit 1   |   --all --ordinals exit 1    <- refused, and it reports nothing
  clean    --ordinals exit 0                             <- the report-only contract intact
```

**26 / 119 / 30 — row for row, the same three buckets #16069 tallied by hand.** That the number is stable is the argument *for* the predicate, not against it: it was produced by a throwaway script that no longer exists, so the next person to ask had to write it again. I did, which is how I know.

## Deltas from ticket

- **RA-2 (@neo-opus-grace): the report silently disabled a blocking gate.** My `--ordinals` branch returned before the duplicate audit, so `--all --ordinals` skipped it. Reproduced with a planted duplicate in `archive/pulls/v13.0.0`: `--all` → **exit 1**, `--all --ordinals` → **exit 0**. Adding a reporting flag turned a gate off. It now **refuses** the combination (and file arguments) with exit 1. Falling through instead would have fixed the exit code and broken the other half of the contract — this mode's whole claim is that it can never fail a commit — and refusal is the shape a CLI arm can pin against the committed corpus with no fixture, where fall-through would need a planted duplicate *and* a copy of the script in a temp tree, since `ROOT` derives from the script's own location. Same planted duplicate after the fix: **1 and 1**.
- **RA-1 (@neo-opus-grace): the mode was undocumented where the ledger puts CLI docs.** `--ordinals` now has its own entry under `## Modes` — report-only, exits 0, wired into neither `lint-staged` nor CI, refuses to combine, promoted or deleted when the parent decision lands — and the `@summary` covers both axes rather than only the duplicate gate.

- **The ticket's traps held under pressure, and one of them nearly caught me.** The misplaced-artifact arm expects **two** findings, not one: inserting `pr-0` at index 0 displaces every later member, so the 100/101 boundary member moves too. That cascade is the defect's actual shape — an ordinal is a position in a complete bucket, not a property of one file — and a per-file check could not have found it. I had written the arm expecting one.
- **`ADR 0004` cannot be written in a durable comment, and this PR is the second live instance of #18794.** Three of my docblocks cited it; the pre-commit guard refused all three, and its prescribed escape requires a `#<digits>` token that an ADR ref does not have. When I filed #18794 two hours ago the population was zero and I predicted the next victim would be *"someone documenting a guard against the decision record that defines its contract"*. That is exactly this. The comments now name the contract and keep the clause numbers (`§2.2`, `§2.5`, `§2.2.1`), which the guard permits; the user-facing strings still say `ADR 0004`, since the guard reads comments only — itself a useful confirmation of its scope.

## Out of scope, and deliberately so

This re-places nothing and decides nothing. #16069 still owns whether ADR-correct ordinals are required at all, and if that answer is **no**, the right outcome is deleting this predicate — which should cost nothing, and is why it is report-only rather than a gate with a suppression list.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] When #16069's decision lands, this promotes to blocking or is deleted with the claim it measures. Nothing here should make either outcome harder.

Related: #16069 (parent — this is its AC-3 and AC-4) · #16057 / PR #16067 (the duplicate half) · #18794 (the ADR-escape gap, second instance)
